newsitem.title: GERMANY: TENNIS-GRAF CRASHES OUT OF GERMAN OPEN.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-GRAF CRASHES OUT OF GERMAN OPEN.

text.p: Former world number one Steffi Graf suffered one of the worst defeats of her career in front of a stadium of stunned home fans in the German Open quarter-finals on Friday.

Playing only her third singles match after three months out with a knee injury, Graf was swept away from the $926,000 tournament 6-0 6-1 by South African Amanda Coetzer, who also knocked the German out of the Australian Open in January.
Graf, who was chasing a record 10th Berlin title, was hoping to make a comeback after losing her number one ranking to Switzerland's Martina Hingis in March, but looked shaky from the outset.
"I was somewhat nervous, because I knew that I couldn't play so well. At the moment I'm 99 per cent away from how I want to be playing," Graf said afterwards.

"After a while I didn't have any self confidence left... I would have been more disappointed if I'd had the feeling it had been a fight," said the 27-year-old, who last lost in Berlin in the 1990 final against Monica Seles.
Coetzer brushed Graf aside in the first set in just 28 minutes. The German got off to a bad start with two double faults in her second service game and missed a break chance in the following game.
Graf ended the match after just 56 minutes with a fifth double fault after losing nine points in a row.
Coetzer, a petite 25-year-old, had encouraging words for Graf, who must now lift her form before this month's French Open.
"She is a really great player. This defeat will spur her on for the French Open rather than depress her," she said. "The defeat will probably take some pressure off her before Paris."
Graf said she was glad she had made her comeback in Berlin. "It was definitely right to go to Berlin, even if I said before that I was not completely fit enough to play," she said.

It was Coetzer's third win in 12 meetings with Graf. She ended the longest match-winning run in professional grand slam history in January when she beat the German top seed 6-2 7-5 on a scorching day at Melbourne Park.
This time Graf had to wait until the fifth game of the second set to win her only game of the match. She made repeated forehand mistakes and never had a grip on the match.
In Saturday's semifinals Coetzer will meet France's Mary Pierce, who beat Croatian Iva Majoli 6-1 6-4 in her quarter-final.
Czech Jana Novotna advanced to meet American Mary Joe Fernandez with a 1-6 6-2 6-0 defeat of Belgium's Sabine Appelmans. Fernandez overcame young Russian Anna Kournikova 6-1 6-4.
